title: Weaving
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Creative Arts; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use a card loom with serrated edges; the phone describes over-under patterns in words.

skills.key_step: The child says the warp runs lengthwise on the loom, the weft goes across over one and under one, and the next row starts opposite.

floor.question: In a paper weave, does each strip go over every strip?

steps: Weave the weft over one, under one.

misconceptions.ask: Which threads are held tight on the loom?
misconceptions.repair: Make a loom and name the threads as they are used: warp stays, weft travels.

listen_for: Over two warp threads and under two
misconceptions.ask: How does a plain weave go?
misconceptions.repair: Weave a strip over one and under one.

listen_for: The same as the first row
misconceptions.ask: How does the second row of a plain weave start?
misconceptions.repair: Weave two rows the same and see the strip fall apart.

misconceptions.ask: Why must the weft not be pulled too tight?
misconceptions.repair: Weave two rows, one too tight; see the waist form.

checks.question: Which threads run lengthwise on the loom?
In plain weave, if row one starts over, how does row two start?
